mission: Explore the bunker's records — partial anchor system data, fragments of the technique lineage. Sera uses Force-lock expertise to access sealed records. First real demonstration of her era-specific value.
why_now: The bunker's records provide context the fortress archive was missing — each node holds a piece of the picture
conflict: The records reference events and concepts Ben has no framework for — the technique lineage is deeper than he expected. Sera translates but her explanation reveals the Jedi Lords were more militaristic and morally compromised than modern Jedi history suggests.
turning_point: Sera cracks a Force-lock in seconds that would take modern Jedi years — her value to the mission becomes undeniable, and Ben's respect shifts from reluctant to genuine
opening_hook: Sera's hands move over the ancient lock mechanism with the ease of someone unlocking their own front door. A thousand years, and her muscle memory is still better than Ben's training.
closing_hook: The records mention Veranthos by name — coordinates, purpose, and a warning notation that Ben can now read. The wound is real. It has a location. And Veraine knows where it is.
emotional_trajectory: Intellectual curiosity -> uncomfortable historical reckoning -> focused urgency

stakes.personal: Ben's growing understanding that modern Jedi education is radically incomplete
stakes.interpersonal: Sera earning her place through competence, not just historical authority
stakes.external: Each fragment of lineage data makes the wound more comprehensible — and more frightening

setting: Battlefield Node bunker — records room, Force-locked archive
sensory_details: The Force-lock dissolving under Sera's touch — a technique Ben has never seen; holographic records in an older data format; the thin place making concentration harder — like reading through slightly wrong glasses
notes: R05 continues (technique lineage progressive revelation). Sera's Force-lock skill is her primary tactical contribution — it provides natural pacing control for archive access and demonstrates her era-specific value beyond moral authority.
